title: Paid SSC CPO (2024) - Idioms PART - (II)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
When I went to Egypt and lost my wallet and passport, I was _____________.
options: 2) putting my nose to the grindstone
3) working my fingers to the bone
4) up in a creek without a paddle
questions.solution: D) Up in a creek without a paddle(idiom) – In a difficult or troublesome situation बिना किसी मदद के मुश्किल स्थिति में

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.
John was always ________ about becoming a millionaire without doing any hard work
options: 1) a storm in a tea cup
4) having an ace up his sleeve
questions.solution: C)Building castles in the air(idiom) – To have unrealistic or impractical dreams or plans. अव्यावहारिक या असंभव सपने देखना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Despite multiple obstacles, she continued with her endeavour, demonstrating that she has nerves of steel
options: 2) An absence of fear or anxiety
4) The capacity to maintain composure when stressed
questions.solution: B)Nerves of steel(idiom) – An absence of fear or anxiety भय या चिंता की अनुपस्थिति

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
It’s Christmas and everything looks so beautiful. It makes me believe that Life is wonderful and pleasant
options: 4) life is a bowl of cherries
questions.solution: D)life is a bowl of cherries(idiom) – life is wonderful and pleasantज़िंदगी आनंदमय और सुखद है

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
We need to make sure that criminals like these get more from the authorities than a very mild punishment
options: 4) a taste of their own medicine
questions.solution: A) a slap on the wrist(idiom) – a very mild punishment बहुत हल्की सज़ा

questions.question:
In question four alternatives are given for the underlined Idiom/Phrase in the sentence.Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
In life, there will be many situations where you have to choose between the devil and the deep blue sea
options: 1) To be in dilemma to choose
2) To be in the deep sea
3) To be in a good condition
questions.solution: A)Between the devil and the deep blue sea(idiom) – To be in dilemma to chooseदुविधा में होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Beat around the bush
options: 3) To avoid talking about what is important.
questions.solution: C)Beat around the bush (idiom)– To avoid talking about what is important. महत्वपूर्ण बात को नजरअंदाज करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I don't know which career he will choose. He delays making strong decisions
options: 2) is as clean as a whistle
questions.solution: A) sits on the fence(idiom) – delays making strong decisions निर्णय लेने में देरी करता है

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined part in the given sentence:
Amar was left in a difficult situation by his business partners
questions.solution: A) High and dry– (in a difficult situation)कठिन परिस्थिति में

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Sacred cow
questions.solution: B)Sacred cow(idiom) – Unquestionableपूजा योग्य

questions.question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.
Have your head in the clouds
options: 1) He had his head in the clouds during an important meeting.
2) The pilot had his head in the clouds while flying a plane.
3) They had their heads in the clouds by looking up at the sky during a meteor shower.
4) She had her head in the clouds by wearing a cloud-shaped hat.
questions.solution: A) Have your head in the clouds(idiom) – To be daydreaming or to be out of touch with reality ख्याली पुलाव बनाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given idiom.
A goose's eye view
questions.solution: D) A bird's eye view(idiom) – A general or comprehensive view or perspective of something from above.चिड़िया की नज़र से देखने का मतलब एक व्यापक या समग्र दृष्टिकोण से देखना।

questions.question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.
He always takes up difficult tasks – those which are beyond his capabilities
options: 2) Bite off more than you can chew
questions.solution: B)Bite off more than you can chew(idiom) – to take on a task that is way too big for someone to handle. अपनी क्षमता से अधिक कठिन कार्य करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Black sheep
questions.solution: C) Black sheep(idiom) – Disreputable बदनाम

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
When pigs fly
options: 1) Something that will never last long
questions.solution: D)When pigs fly(idiom) – Something that will never happen कभी नहीं होने वाली चीज़

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the options to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.
After his business failed, he had to reduce spending and adjust to a frugal lifestyle
options: 2) hit the nail on the head
3) let the cat out of the bag
questions.solution: A) tighten his belt–had to reduce spendingखर्च में कटौती करनी पड़ी

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Make waves
questions.solution: A)Make waves(idiom) – To cause difficulty or create a significant impact in a situation. मुसीबत खड़ी करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
I sometimes accept excess work to please my manager, so I take more responsibilities than one can manage.
options: 1) get a taste of my own medicine
3) hear it straight from the horse’s mouth
4) bite off more than I can chew
questions.solution: D) bite off more than I can chew(idiom) – Take on more than one can handle जितना संभाल सकते हैं उससे अधिक जिम्मेदारियां लेना

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Back to back
options: 1) Something follows immediately after something else.
3) Present and discuss the details of something.
4) Do something very fast or with great energy
questions.solution: A) Back to back(idiom) – Something follows immediately after something else किसी चीज़ के तुरंत बाद कुछ और होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
The best of both worlds
options: 2) Stay strong in a difficult situation
questions.solution: D)The best of both worlds(idiom) – Good in every way हर तरह से अच्छा
